I was so focused on my own pain that I had a hard time recognizing my SO was actually depressed. Plus, it manifests so differently for men and women. After I recognized it, I still couldn't understand it. And maybe I didn't want to, because it would distract me from my own sadness. A couple days ago, he said some things that finally led me to understand, to the point where I really, deeply emotionally, felt his pain. But now, I am already having trouble maintaining that remembrance, having sunk into mild depression again.

When I get in a suicidal mind frame, I only think of my pain. I don't consider how purportedly ending my pain would affect others. Sometimes I truly don't think of it; others I dismiss it quickly without processing it, disguise it by claiming no one actually cares, or cruelly say that I really don't care how I hurt others with my suicide. Sometimes I even vilify others and claim they deserve it.

Seeing as I barely understand his depression, I realize he easily may not know mine either, especially since I hold back so much on discussing it.

It angers me that anyone in my life might consider suicide. Because they are highly valuable people with even more unused potential and there are three thousand and two ways around their problem and gee did you ever think of the effect on me? Yet when I consider it for myself, it's suddenly so much more acceptable...

I'm not shaming but rather pointing out a hypocrisy in our flawed way of thinking. A cycle of stubbornly selfish, self-pleasing sadness. Which perhaps breaks when we force ourselves to consider and do something for somebody else's happiness.
I'm depressed myself, but I think we're dangerously self-absorbed. Depression ultimately is unproductive rumination focused inwardly. An inability to recognize/understand/acknowledge others' pain.

Depression so often exists with a terrible narcissism, and there are so many flaws in our thinking. Some depression exists to cause the person to examine something painful, and it persists for a long as they avoid that thing. If you're hiding from some fact, some truth, some incident, the depression will keep coming back, urging you to address the problem.
